title: evacuation-controller: safe-node-evacuation + terra-helm hooks for multi-AZ failover
author: Anya Patel
description: Motivation: private deployments need an automated, auditable evacuation/failover primitive that can be invoked by runbooks or by automated health-routing. This PR adds an evacuation-controller CRD + controller, Terraform hooks to wire evacuation policies into VPC routing modules, and a Helm chart subchart that provides a safe-drain lifecycle hook and cluster-level evacuation policy UI; it also wires in a chaos-ready toggle for DR drills. Changes include controller logic for fencing and cordon+drain with per-pod skip annotations, a transactional state machine persisted in the cluster configmap for resume/rollback, terraform module updates to populate cloud-route-weights and healthcheck targets, and a helm pre-upgrade job that performs preflight validation and creates a snapshot for rollback. Summary of intent: - provide a first-class API for planned evacuation (operator-managed) - enable automated failover from automation tools (runbooks/incident playbooks) - ensure resumable evacuations and safe rollback in case of partial failures What this PR contains: - CRD: EvacuationPlan (spec: targets, mode: graceful|force, drainTimeoutSecs, skipSelectors, rollbackPolicy) - controller: reconcile loop, fencing integration (cloud provider tagging), KV-backed plan state, and metrics/traces - helm: new subchart redwood-evacuator with templates, pre-upgrade job, and optional chaos toggle - terraform: module network/route updates, IAM role policy addition, and a small helper that creates a runbook S3 object with the plan JSON - tests: unit coverage for controller state transitions, integration tests that spin up a kind cluster and mock cloud route weights - docs: runbook-as-code examples and a sample Linear workflow which ties an on-call action to an evacuation plan Checklist: - [x] CRD + controller implementation - [x] Helm chart and preflight hooks - [x] Terraform module changes and examples - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and runbook example - [x] Security review notes (IAM minimization) Backwards compatibility and rollout: the EvacuationPlan CRD is additive; controller is deployed behind a feature flag in helm (enabled=false by default). Terraform changes add optional variables with sensible defaults; no existing resources mutated unless the operator is enabled. Operational notes: the operator exposes metrics (evacuation_duration_seconds, plan_state_count) and a /debug/state endpoint for debugging; we included a small CLI script in examples/evacuate.sh that wraps kubectl apply + terraform run to coordinate a runbook. Related: ENG-6123 (DR automation primer), SUP-1421 (customer reported partial failover during AZ outage). Impact on CI: added an integration job which is gated behind a DR label to keep regular PR cycles fast. Merge strategy: squash merge to keep controller internals tidy.

review_comments: Marcus Chen: Please add more explicit unit tests around the resume path when a controller pod restarts. The state machine needs strong test coverage.
Anya Patel: Added tests and a failing-to-successful resume scenario in the integration suite; see test/integration/evacuation_test.go commit.
Lena Ortiz: Can the terraform change be feature-flagged so existing installs don't flip route weights unless operator is enabled? Also request to reduce IAM scope for the runbook S3 helper.
Anya Patel: Terraform variables are optional and default to no-op; updated IAM to use least privilege and added a note in security/iam/evacuation-role.json.
Omar Reyes: Ran helm upgrade on a staging cluster; preflight job caught a missing node label and failed safely which is the desired behaviour. Approved.
release_notes: Add EvacuationPlan operator and infrastructure hooks for automated multi-AZ evacuation and DR drills; introduces helm subchart 'redwood-evacuator' and optional terraform variables to integrate route weights and runbook artifacts.
